title: Grateful Dead Live at Strand Lyceum on 1972-05-25
source: SBD -> Master Reel 10 inch reels recorded at 7.5 ips (1/2 track) -> Apogee AD500 D-> Dat/0 (48k) D

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of the fiery 5/25/72 London show with a smoking Good Lovin' jam, soaring Uncle John's Band and powerful Wharf Rat, presented in an excellent mix despite missing parts of the second set.
ai_review.review: The recording is a high‑quality soundboard tape that showcases the band on fire – Jerry’s guitar is in top form, Keith’s piano adds bright accents and Pigpen’s organ/voice shines on Good Lovin'.  Highlights include a monster Uncle John's Band > Wharf Rat sequence and an emotional final Sittin’ on Top of the World, although the second‑set conclusion is absent.  Overall the performance is energetic and memorable, with only a few weaker moments such as a flat Casey Jones and a less‑focused Dark Star.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews are 5‑star, praising both the musical performance and the sound quality; only a few note minor flaws or missing portions, leading to a strong positive overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced mix with clear piano/organ separation and strong guitar presence; the only technical limitation is the incomplete second‑set capture.

standout_songs: Sittin' on Top of the World
show_quality.setlist_flow: A slow‑burning first set that builds into a high‑energy second set; the band hits several peaks before the tape cuts out after Sugar Magnolia, leaving the finale missing.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his finest‑era guitar tone and soaring solos; his vocal work on the final ballad is noted as especially emotive.
band_member_comments.Phil: Mixed feedback – some reviewers highlight interesting, bass‑driven jams in Dark Star, while others feel he never 'unleashes' full muscle here.
band_member_comments.Bob: Acknowledged for strong rhythm guitar and organ interplay, particularly on Good Lovin' where his organ counterpoint shines.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano is described as grand, excited (double trills) and adds the final touches that fire up the band.
